title: A higher early-curiosity score went with longer looks at impossible events
summary: In a study of 47 infants, a higher score on an early curiosity scale went with a stronger looking preference for physically impossible events.
body: Lee, Lazaro, Wang, Şen, Lucca, and colleagues tested 47 infants, average age about 17 months, ranging from about 10 to 25 months. They report that looking preference for physically impossible events was positively associated with the Early Multidimensional Curiosity Scale, and was not associated with temperament, vocabulary, or the caregiver's own trait curiosity. Across event types the average preference for the impossible outcome was only marginal. The solidity event on its own, an object seeming to pass through a barrier, did show a preference. The paper was published 2 February 2023 in Frontiers in Psychology. It describes the infants who were tested. It is not a screen for a particular child.

sources.title: Exploring individual differences in infants' looking preferences for impossible events
sources.author: Nayen Lee, Vanessa Lazaro, Jinjing Jenny Wang, Hilal H. Şen, Kelsey Lucca, and colleagues
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Frontiers in Psychology article, 2 February 2023. Paraphrase of Study 1: N = 47, the EMCS association, a marginal average preference across event types, and a clear solidity-event preference. No sentence is copied.
